source: Quiz 4 - Sessions 1-5: Building and Improving Agent Skills
question: Why do successful recurrent-depth experiments leave the benefit of extra passes on a different model uncertain?

options.text: Matching parameter counts is enough to transfer the measured improvement.
options.feedback: Parameter count describes learned numerical values, not whether another model was trained to benefit from recurrent processing. The tested architecture and task matter.

options.text: Reusing fixed weights makes additional passes equivalent to a single pass.
options.feedback: Fixed weights can act on changing hidden representations. Reuse permits extra computation, but its benefit still needs evidence.

options.text: The length of a printed explanation determines the useful number of passes.
options.feedback: Visible text is an incomplete measure of hidden numerical computation. It cannot establish how much recurrent processing helps a different model.

options.text: The benefit depends on the model, its training, and the task.
options.feedback: The research demonstrates a trained approach, not a general improvement from adding loops to an arbitrary model. Evaluate the amount of processing that helps in the intended setting.
